chapters.title: Animal Behavior
chapters.sourcePressure: The source uses primate grooming and Arabian babbler helping to teach readers to separate a behavior's useful surface from its hidden social payoff.
chapters.coreMove: Ask what social payoff a useful behavior buys before accepting its surface function as the whole explanation.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer turns the animal examples into sneering proof that care and cooperation are fake.
mustNotDriftInto: human office politics before the animal analogy lands

chapters.title: Competition
chapters.sourcePressure: The source frames human behavior as shaped by intra-group competition across sex, status, and politics, with signaling as the shared logic.
chapters.coreMove: Sort social behavior by the partner market it addresses: mates, friends, or coalition allies.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer reduces competition to ruthless individualism and loses the signal logic that makes cooperation competitive too.

chapters.title: Norms
chapters.sourcePressure: The source explains norms as collectively enforced rules that let groups suppress visible selfishness through coalition pressure, gossip, and reputation.
chapters.coreMove: Treat a norm as a rule backed by group enforcement, then ask what visible selfishness it makes costly.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer treats norms as polite values instead of enforced social technology.

chapters.title: Cheating
chapters.sourcePressure: The source shows cheating as norm-breaking that survives under thin cover when accusation, proof, and common knowledge are hard to assemble.
chapters.coreMove: Look for the thin cover that keeps a visible violation below the threshold for coordinated punishment.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer treats cheating as secret villainy instead of public ambiguity protected by enforcement costs.

chapters.title: Self-Deception
chapters.sourcePressure: The source presents self-deception as more than inner comfort: hidden truths can be kept from the self to make outward signals more convincing.
chapters.coreMove: Separate felt sincerity from full self-knowledge, then ask what social signal the ignorance protects.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer turns self-deception into therapy talk or conscious lying with a nicer label.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Reasons
chapters.sourcePressure: The source argues that people fabricate counterfeit reasons after the fact, with split-brain and confabulation evidence supporting the press-secretary model of the ego.
chapters.coreMove: Treat the stated reason as a press release and inspect what decision it was written to justify.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer turns counterfeit reasons into ordinary excuses and misses post-hoc confabulation.

chapters.title: Body Language
chapters.sourcePressure: The source treats body language as honest signaling that coordinates sensitive behavior in sex, politics, and status when words are too easy to fake or too costly to use.
chapters.coreMove: Read nonverbal behavior as costly coordination where words would be cheap, risky, or too explicit.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer drifts into pop microexpression decoding instead of honest signaling in sensitive social games.

chapters.title: Laughter
chapters.sourcePressure: The source treats laughter as a play signal that softens physical or social danger and preserves deniability in risky interaction.
chapters.coreMove: Use laughter to identify when people are making danger playable while keeping a retreat route open.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer makes laughter about happiness or humor quality instead of danger, play, and deniability.

chapters.title: Conversation
chapters.sourcePressure: The source argues that conversation is not only information exchange; it also displays the ability to know and learn, including in news and academic research.
chapters.coreMove: Listen for knowledge display inside talk that claims to be only information exchange.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer turns conversation into communication tips and misses status display around knowing and learning.

chapters.title: Consumption
chapters.sourcePressure: The source widens conspicuous consumption into consumer signaling, where purchases communicate wealth, conscientiousness, adventurousness, and identity.
chapters.coreMove: Decode purchases as signals of traits, not only as satisfaction of needs or wealth display.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer makes the chapter only about luxury status and misses conscientiousness, adventurousness, and identity signals.
mustNotDriftInto: brand case study with invented data

chapters.title: Art
chapters.sourcePressure: The source reads art through costly signaling and the handicap principle, where impracticality and extrinsic features help signal value.
chapters.coreMove: Ask how difficulty, waste, and external validation make artistic value legible as a costly signal.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer turns art into personal expression or taste debate and misses costly signaling.

chapters.title: Charity
chapters.sourcePressure: The source argues that charity often signals wealth, empathy, and prosocial orientation, so giving patterns can fit social display better than pure effectiveness.
chapters.coreMove: Evaluate giving as help plus public signal, then ask whether visibility is serving impact or the giver.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer turns charity into hypocrisy or effective-altruism math and loses mixed motives.

chapters.title: Education
chapters.sourcePressure: The source argues that education signals intelligence, conscientiousness, and conformity while also serving babysitting, networking, indoctrination, and domestication functions.
chapters.coreMove: Read schooling as instruction plus certification of intelligence, discipline, and institutional fit.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer argues school is useless and ignores real learning plus the broader signaling bundle.

chapters.title: Medicine
chapters.sourcePressure: The source frames medicine partly as conspicuous caring, where visible sacrifice and public signs of care matter alongside health claims.
chapters.coreMove: Ask what care a treatment visibly displays in addition to what health effect it may produce.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer turns medicine into placebo theater or anti-medical cynicism.

chapters.title: Religion
chapters.sourcePressure: The source frames religion as group bonding, loyalty display, and norm enforcement through sacrifice, ritual synchrony, badges, sermons, and supernatural enforcement.
chapters.coreMove: Look at religious practice as belief plus visible loyalty, shared rhythm, and norm enforcement.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer reduces religion to false belief or manipulative control and loses sincere bonding.

chapters.title: Politics
chapters.sourcePressure: The source frames democratic politics as policy pursuit plus visible group loyalty, making strong emotions, low information, and sacrifice easier to explain.
chapters.coreMove: Interpret political action as side-taking that can signal loyalty even when policy knowledge is thin.
chapters.commonMisread: The writer turns politics into voter stupidity or partisan scolding instead of mixed policy and loyalty motives.
